question:
A safety professional must select a respirator for employees working in an inert
atmosphere. Which type of respirator is appropriate?
explanation:
Inert atmospheres contain no oxygen. Air purifying respirators are inadequate in this
instance because they do not supply oxygen. Negative pressure air supplied
respirators will expose employees to the oxygen deficient atmospheres if there is a leak
in the respirator seal.
The correct solution is D.

elevator on the 16th floor of their hotel and presses the button for the lobby. While they

floor will the elevator stop and discharge its passengers?

options.a: Lobby marked “L” on the elevator panel
options.b: Garage marked “G” on the elevator panel
options.c: First floor marked “1” on the elevator panel
options.d: Second floor marked “2*” where the * is a star on the elevator panel.

explanation:
Elevator panels always have a floor marked with a star. This floor is the floor of primary
recall in the event a fire is detected in the building.
The correct solution is D.

question:

on risk minimization within the culture of a manufacturing company?

question:
A safety professional hired an industrial hygienist to evaluate the exposure to
hexavalent chromium by welders. The report from the industrial hygienist indicated the
welders were exposed to an average of 0.5 mg/m3. The OSHA PEL is 0.005 mg/m3.
Which type of respirator would be appropriate for the welders?
explanation:
The protection factors for respirators are:
Half-face air purifying respirator = 10
Full-face air purifying respirator = 50
Loose-fitting powered air purifying respirator = 25
Tight-fitting powered air purifying respirator = 1000
The Maximum Use Concentration (MUC) = PEL x Protection Factor (PF)
We need an MUC equal to or greater than the exposure of 0.5 mg/m3.
Solve for the PF: MUC = PEL x PF
0.5 mg/m3 = 0.005 mg/m3 x PF
PF = 100
The tight-fitting PAPR is the only respirator listed above with a PF greater than 100.
The correct solution is D.

question:
A safety professional from the United States will be teaching a class in Europe. She will
be taking her laptop computer with her, and she is concerned about the power
requirements of her machine. The power supply that came with the laptop has the
following information written on the label:
INPUT: 100-240V~ 1.6A(1.6A) 50-60Hz
OUTPUT: 19V 3.42A(3.42A) 65W
What type of power transformer does the safety professional need to purchase for her
laptop?
explanation:
Electrical distributions vary in different parts of the world.
Electricity in the U.S.A. is generally delivered to the power outlet at 110 V and 60 Hz.
Electricity in Europe is generally delivered to the power outlet at 220 V and 50 Hz.
The power supply on the safety professional’s computer is capable of accepting a range
of power inputs from 100 to 240 V and 50 – 60 Hz.
She will need an adapter to fit her electrical cord into the European outlet.
The correct solution is D.

question:
Engineers are designing a new rocket to carry people to the moon. After the initial
design is complete, they will evaluate each component to determine what is likely to
happen in the event the component fails. What is this type of analysis called?
explanation:
A hazard and operability study identifies hazards and operability problems.
Failure modes and effects analysis evaluates how the failure of each system component
will affect the entire system.
What-if analysis is a loosely structured brainstorming exercise to identify situations that
may cause system failure.
Fault tree analysis is a systematic approach of evaluating specific failures. The analysis
starts with the fault and works backwards identify all conditions that will eventually lead
to the fault. The analysis uses Boolean logic to determine the probability of the failure.
The correct solution is B.

question:
Which type of radiation produces the most damage in a person when it interacts directly
with living tissue?

options.d: It depends on the energy level.

explanation:
Alpha radiation is not a threat when it is outside the body; however, it produces
significant damage when interacting directly with living tissue inside the body.
The correct solution is A.

question:
A system has three components in series. The failure of any of the components will
cause the system to fail. The failure rate of each component is 0.05. What is the
overall expected failure rate of the system?
explanation:
P(system failure) = 1 – P(system success)
P(system success) = P(component 1 success) x P(component 2 success) x P(component 3 success)
P(system success) = 0.95 x 0.95 x 0.95 = 0.857
P(system failure) = 1 – 0.857 = 0.143
The correct solution is B.

question:
A general rule of thumb in office safety is to not store materials closer than 18” to the
ceiling. What is the purpose of this rule?

options.a: This allows sprinklers to reach all combustible materials.
options.b: This prevents people from materials falling on people.
options.c: This prevents people from using inadequate platforms (office chairs) to reach objects.
options.d: There is no such rule of thumb.

explanation:
The National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) standards require materials to be
stored in such a manner as to not disturb the water flow from sprinkler heads. The
actual distance below the sprinklers is dependent on the distance to the sprinkler.
A good rule of thumb is to keep all materials at least 18” away from the ceiling.
The correct solution is A.

question: Which of the following is an appropriate control for heat stress?

options.a: Encourage workers to drink small amounts of water about every 20 minutes
options.b: Allow employees to self-limit exposure to heat
options.c: Remove workers from hot environments when core body temperatures exceed 38.5o C
options.d: All of the above are appropriate heat stress controls

explanation:
Here is a list of general controls for heat stress1:
• Provide instructions and training about heat stress and strain
• Encourage drinking small amounts of water about every 20 minutes
• Permit self-limitation of heat exposure
• Counsel and monitor workers on certain medications
• Encourage healthy life-styles
• Adjust expectations of workers returning to work after an absence
• Consider pre-placement medical screening for employees
• Monitor heat stress conditions
Here is a list of indications of excessive heat strain1:
• Sustained heart rate in excess of 180 bpm minus worker’s age (180 – age)
• Core body temperature greater than 38.5 oC (101.3 oF)
• Recovery heart rate greater than 120 bpm
• Symptoms of sudden and severe fatigue
The correct solution is D.

control?

materials in an air “pocket”.
Dilution ventilation is not appropriate for highly toxic contaminants.

options.d: Treat with an autoclave or 15% bleach, seal in plastic bio-bag, and incinerate

Biohazardous animal tissue is incinerated. Prior to incineration, all materials are treated
to kill pathogens.

question:

past twenty years?

options.a: Employees that smoke cigarettes have become a common cause of propped- open doors.

options.d: Distances to local fire departments are increasing.

explanation:
Smoking policies have changed significantly in the last 20 years. It is usually no longer
acceptable to smoke in the workplace. This forces many employees to smoke outside.
It is relatively common for employees to prop open exits to allow easy access for
smoking outside.
The correct solution is A.

Which of the following organs and tissue is most sensitive to whole-body ionizing

explanation:

ionizing radiation.
Red bone marrow is generates blood cells. Red bone marrow is most sensitive to
ionizing radiation of the choices offered.

explanation:
Fungus grows well when the relative humidity is greater than 60%.
The correct solution is D.

that _______

explanation:
Active training requires that students do most of the work. They are active (doing
something) in the learning process.
The correct solution is D.

question: Select the correct definition for the heat stress index.

options.a: The ratio of relative humidity to absolute humidity.
options.b: The ratio of wet bulb temperature to dry bulb temperature.
options.c: The ratio of the evaporative heat loss required to maintain body temperature to the maximum evaporative heat loss.

explanation:
The heat stress index is the evaporative heat loss required to maintain body
temperature divided by the maximum available heat loss through evaporation.
The correct solution is C.

question:
Which fire extinguisher should be used on a trash can full of paper ignited by a
cigarette?
explanation:
Class A fire extinguishers are used on ordinary combustible materials.
Class B fire extinguishers are used on combustible liquids.
Class C fire extinguishers are used for electrical fires.
Class K fire extinguishers are used for commercial kitchen fires.
The correct solution is A.

question:
A U. S. consumer is taken ill from eating a raw cookie dough product contaminated with
e coli. The package states that the cookie dough must be baked before being
consumed. The manufacturer has no quality control procedures in place to ensure that
e coli is not present. The consumer sues the manufacturer to cover lost wages and
medical expenses while being ill. What type of liability is the plaintiff likely to cite in their
lawsuit?

options.a: There is no basis for the lawsuit. The manufacturer is clearly not liable based on the package information.
options.b: The plaintiff is likely to claim that the manufacturer violated an express warranty because the product made no mention of the possibility that e coli could be present.
options.c: The plaintiff is likely to claim that the manufacturer was strictly liable because the e coli was present and made him sick.
options.d: The plaintiff is likely to claim that the manufacturer was negligent because the manufacturer should have anticipated the possibility that the product would be eaten raw by some consumers.

explanation:
The manufacturer did not make a specific claim that the cookie dough will not contain e
coli. The manufacturer did not violate an express warranty.
The plaintiff may make a strictly liable claim, but the plaintiff is more likely to claim
negligence. Raw cookie dough is frequently consumed in the United States, and many
ice cream products include raw cookie dough as a major ingredient. The court would
likely hold that a manufacturer should reasonably anticipate the product would be eaten
raw (think about children getting into the refrigerator), and the manufacturer should have
taken steps to ensure e coli is not present in the product.
The correct solution is D.

options.d: Determine the probability of a negative event

explanation:
The job safety analysis (JSA) can be an effective tool to minimize hazards in an existing
task through awareness and training of employees. The JSA is often completed by an
employee experienced in performing the task.

A 35 year old man is shoveling sand on a construction site during a hot summer day.
The man takes a 10 minute break once every hour. What is the maximum sustained
heart rate for the man which will not indicate he is becoming overstressed?
explanation:
The ACGIH recommends sustained heart rate should not exceed (180 – age) in bpm. I
180 – 35 = 145 bpm.
The correct solution is C.

question:
A safety manager observed an employee on the floor without hearing protection in an
area that is clearly posted that hearing protection is required. What is the best response
of the safety manager?

options.c: Speak directly with the employee’s supervisor about the issue.
options.d: Wait until the safety meeting next week, and speak about it privately with the employee’s supervisor.

explanation:
Safety is a line responsibility. It is the supervisor’s responsibility to ensure their
employees are working in a safe manner.
Behaviors are more likely to be modified if the feedback regarding the behavior is
provided in a timely manner. It is important to minimize delay in providing feedback.
The correct solution is C.

A worker must push a wooden pallet across a rough finish concrete floor. The wooden
with materials weighs 40 lbs and it has a footprint of 4 square feet. The coefficient of
static friction between the wood and rough finish concrete floor is 0.62. How much force
must the worker use to keep the pallet moving?
explanation:

when the surface is horizontal.

However, the problem should have given the coefficient of kinetic friction because the
pallet is moving. The surface area is not used in this problem.

question:
A safety professional is attending a safety conference in a large city. His hotel room is
on the 12th floor. One day while riding the elevator up to his room, a fire alarm is
activated in the hotel. What is the elevator likely to do?

options.a: Stop at the 12th floor and open the door and lock in this position.
options.b: Proceed to the floor with the shortest path to the nearest exit discharge, and open the door and lock in this position.
options.c: Stop immediately and open the doors so passengers can discharge and enter a stairwell to exit the building and lock in this position.
options.d: Stop at the nearest floor and open the doors so passengers can discharge and enter a stairwell, and lock in this position.

explanation:
Elevators are designed to return to the floor of primary recall if a fire is detected. The
floor of primary recall will be the floor that is closes to an exit discharge. This floor will
have a star by its number on the elevator control panel.
If the fire is detected on the floor of primary recall, then the elevator will stop at
secondary floor (often one floor above or below).
The correct solution is B.

A community theater group created a haunted house as a fundraiser during Halloween
this year. The haunted house used large quantities of dry ice to create a fog effect in
the mummy room of the house. Which of the following procedures should NOT be done
when working with the dry ice?

options.a: Keep the dry ice in a tightly sealed container.
options.b: Handle the dry ice with gloved hands.
options.c: Use the dry ice in a well-ventilated area.
options.d: Wear safety goggles when handling dry ice.

explanation:
Dry ice has a vapor pressure of 56.5 atm. Storing dry ice in a sealed container will likely
cause the container to explode.
The correct solution is A.

question: Which of the following is most important when developing a training lesson plan?
explanation:
Health and safety training must include measureable objectives. The objectives
describe what the trainees will learn from the training. It is the starting point for lesson
plan development.
The correct solution is C.

question: Which US industry has the highest work-related fatality rate?
explanation:
According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, agriculture, forestry, fishing and
hunting had a fatality rate of 30.5 per 100,000 workers in 2004. The construction fatality
rate in 2004 was 12.0 per 100,000 workers, the transportation and warehousing fatality
rate was 18.0 per 100,000 workers and the utilities fatality rate was 6.1 per 100,000
workers.
The correct solution is A.
Mining is also very dangerous. The fatality rate of mining in 2004 was 28.3
occupational fatalities per 100,000 workers.

question:
A safety professional was preparing Thanksgiving dinner for a group of friends. An
exhaust fan was installed above his stove to provide exhaust for the emissions from the
stove. What type of hood was used to capture and remove these emissions?
explanation:
A slot hood is used on the side of an open surface tank.
A canopy hood is a receiving hood. It tanks advantage of the upward inertia from hot
gases.
A plain hood is a plain opening end of duct.
An enclosing hood encloses the generating source.
The correct solution is B.

question: Which is the first event in a product liability lawsuit?
explanation:
The complaint is the filing of the lawsuit.
Discovery is the process of searching for and evaluating evidence.
The trial is process of both sides presenting their case in court.
A settlement may be reached at any time before a verdict. Many cases are settled
before trial, but not all cases reach a settlement.
The correct solution is A.

policies and objectives in an organization.

health problems?
explanation:

• Static loads

• Vibration

Management, Second Edition, AIHA Press. Fairfax, VA. 2003.

question:
Which of the following is the least important consideration when determining the
location of a nuclear power plant?
explanation:
There are many variables to consider when determining the location of an industrial
facility. Companies need to evaluate the safety of the surrounding population, proximity
to transportation corridors and access to a stable employee base as well as many
others.
Nuclear power plants have the potential of causing catastrophic harm if things were to
go very bad. Examples include Three Mile Island in the U.S. and Chernobyl in the
former Soviet Union (now Ukraine).
It is important to protect nuclear facilities from potential natural disasters (e.g.
earthquakes) and minimize potential exposures to large populations. Security of the
facility is also extremely important. The least important consideration of the listed
options is the value of the land.

question:

negligence lawsuit?

negligent in that duty.

question: The Pareto Principle states that…

options.a: The majority of all accidents are caused by human error.
options.b: 80% of all problems come from 20% of the causes.
options.c: Time, distance, and shielding are the foundation of radiation protection
options.d: The probability of success is based upon the continuance of maintenance.

explanation:
The Pareto Principle (80-20 rule) states that 80% of all problems (i.e. effects) come from
20% of the causes. This principle has applicability in safety, economics, populations,
etc.
The correct solution is B.

question: Which solution describes claims-made insurance?

options.a: Coverage that applies to liabilities incurred and asserted during the policy period.
options.b: Coverage after the termination of the policy that applies to liabilities that occur during the policy period.
options.c: Coverage after the termination of the policy for liabilities that occur after the policy period.
options.d: Coverage that applies to liabilities during the policy period and for a period of 10 years after termination of the policy.

explanation:
Occurrence insurance covers incidents that occur during the policy period. The policy in
force on the date of the event must cover the loss.
Claims made insurance covers incidents based on the date that the insured becomes
aware of the claim and notifies the insurance carrier.
The correct solution is A.

question: Which three gases are typically evaluated in a confined space before entry?
explanation:
Oxygen deficiency and explosive atmospheres are significant hazards in confined
spaces. Carbon monoxide is also likely to be present from nearby combustion sources.

question:
A company rents inflatable bouncing rooms to be used at children birthday parties. The
rental company includes a waiver for the parent to sign that the parent will not sue the
company if a child is injured while using the device. What is the main purpose of the
waiver?

options.a: The main purpose is to create a legal document protecting the company from strict liability lawsuits.
options.b: The main purpose is to create a legal document protecting the company from frivolous lawsuits.
options.c: The main purpose is to create a legal document protecting the company negligence lawsuits.
options.d: The main purpose is to inform the parent of the risk associated with using the device.

explanation:
Parents cannot give away or sign away the rights of their children. If a child is injured
due to the negligence of another party, they have a right seek compensation for their
injuries.
The correct solution is D.

question:
Which of the following system safety analysis techniques may lead to an estimation of
the probability of a catastrophic event?
explanation:

the probability of the event.
Preliminary hazard analysis is a first look of the potential hazards of a product under
development.
Failure modes and effect analysis evaluates the potential effects from equipment failure.
The correct solution is B.

question: What is the most common type of workplace eye injury?
explanation:
Foreign bodies are the most common type of physical injury to the eye. Cataracts can
be occupationally caused by: ionizing radiation, ultraviolet radiation, infrared radiation,
foreign bodies, and chemicals.
The correct solution is B.

question:
Which of the following are not included in the “Seven Cardinal Rules of Risk
Communication” established by the US EPA?

options.a: Meet the needs of the media
options.c: Accept and involve the public/other consumers as legitimate partners
options.d: Coordinate and collaborate only with others who agree with your view

explanation:
For effective risk communication, you should coordinate and collaborate with other
credible sources, not only people who agree with your view point. In addition to a, b,
and c, you should:
1. Be honest, frank, and open
2. Listen to the publics specific concerns
3. Plan carefully and evaluate your efforts with a focus on your strengths,
weaknesses, opportunities, and threats.
Source: Covello, Vincent T.; Allen., Frederick H. (April 1988). Seven
Cardinal Rules of Risk Communication. Washington, DC: U.S.
Environmental Protection Agency. OPA-87-020.
The correct solution is D.

question:

noise exposure?

options.a: Issue hearing protection devices with an NRR greater than 5 to the worker

options.c: Build an enclosure around the server to contain the noise
options.d: Change the orientation of the server to direct the noise in a different direction

explanation:
The generally accepted hierarchy of controls is provided below:
Elimination of hazard
Substitution (of a less hazardous substance)
Engineering controls
Administrative controls
Personal protective equipment

should be tried first.

over 8 hours.
The number one cause of occupational fatalities is motor vehicle accidents.

question: What is the primary purpose of the ANSI/AIHA Z10 standard?

question: Which statement best describes a “What-If” analysis?

options.a: It is an informal investigative method of evaluating hypothetical situations.
options.b: It is a formal, systematic, logical and structured method to evaluate potential deviations of operations or design standards.
options.c: It is a formal method of evaluating the effects of possible failures in a system.
options.d: It is a structured deductively reasoned analysis to determine what events that may lead to a catastrophic event. B ow e n E H S , I nc .

explanation:
A “what-if” analysis is an informal method of evaluating hypothetical situations.

possible failures in a system.
A fault tree analysis is a structured deductively reasoned analysis to determine what
events that may lead to a catastrophic event.

question:
A retailer sold bread that was labeled as “Gluten Free”. Unfortunately, the bread was
made with wheat flour and contained large amounts of gluten. The retailer knew the
bread actually contained gluten. Customers with celiac disease that consumed the
bread became very sick. Which liability theory may be used to sue the retailer?

options.d: All of the above B ow e n E H S , I nc .

explanation:
A warranty claim is appropriate when the product does not meet performance standards
as advertised or specifically stated by the seller.
A negligence claim is appropriate when a buyer was harmed by a deficient product, and
the seller knew (or should have known) of the deficiency and took no action. The
deficiency must have existed at the time it left the control of the seller.
A strict liability claim is appropriate when a product causes harm regardless of whether
the seller knew about the deficiency.
Some product liability claims may be filed under multiple theories.
The correct solution is D.
B ow e n E H S , I nc .

question: What is one of the benefits of using a quiz at the end of a safety training lesson?

options.a: A quiz can be written to ensure everyone answers all questions correctly and documents that the lesson objectives are met.

An anonymous Certified Safety Professional (CSP) was working on a home
improvement project during the recent holiday weekend. The CSP was installing a
coaxial cable running from his living room wall to the attic. This cable would connect an
attic antenna to the television receiver in the living room. This installation involved
drilling a hole from the crawlspace into the interior of the wall in which the coaxial
connector was to be installed. The CSP knew it was critical to correctly position himself
in the crawlspace.
Unfortunately, the anonymous CSP drilled his first hole directly into a stud. The second
hole he drilled missed the wall entirely and came through into the floor of the doorway
between the hall and the living room. At this point, the anonymous CSP realized he had
incorrectly positioned himself in the crawlspace. His third attempt was successful.
When the anonymous CSP explained to his wife that he made an error, she merely
shrugged and asked if he could fix it. She did not yell or chastise him in any way.
What risk assessment error was made by the CSP?

options.d: Failure to use personal protective equipment

The correct solution is B.

question:
Which of the following substances is likely to produce a violent reaction if inadvertently
mixed with a strong solution of lye?
explanation:
Lye is a common name for sodium hydroxide, a strong base. Concentrated solutions of
strong bases are chemically incompatible with strong acids, in that the reaction of a
strong base with a strong acid can result in the generation of high temperatures,
spattering, and/or container swelling or bursting. Muriatic acid is a common name for
hydrochloric acid (HCl), a strong acid. Sodium hypochlorite is the chemical name for
what is commonly known as chlorine bleach, which produces a basic (pH > 7) solution
in water. Potassium chloride is a salt. Baking soda is the common name for sodium
bicarbonate, which produces a basic solution in water. Of the given choices, only
muriatic acid will produce hazardous reaction with lye. The key to correctly answering
this problem is having familiarity with the common and chemical names of the
substances, as well as knowledge of the chemical characteristics of each.
The correct solution is D.

question:
Which root cause analysis method relies upon creation of a graphical “fishbone”
diagram showing the influencing factors in the causation of an incident?
explanation:
Construction of Ishikawa cause-and-effect diagrams is a quality improvement technique
used to help identify the influencing factors that lead to a particular outcome. These
diagrams are called “fishbone” diagrams because of their appearance. FMEA, or
Failure Mode Effects Analysis, is a system safety engineering technique for anticipation
of the impacts to system reliability due to a particular event. 5-Why is a investigative
“drill-down” technique that involves successive questioning of why a particular event
occurred. FHA, Fault Hazard Analysis, is a system safety method for anticipating
hazards that may result from a single-fault events.
The correct solution is B.

question:
Aunt Mavis is an accomplished safety professional and an avid fan of football: she
wears face paint in her favorite team’s colors while watching every game, whether
watching from the stadium or from the couch at home. Last year, during the annual
Thanksgiving football extravaganza that always follows the big feast at Aunt Mavis’
house, a very low flying and apparently blind migrating goose collided with the satellite
TV dish. The impact of the big bird misaligned the dish and caused a loss of reception
during the final few minutes of the big game. Aunt Mavis quickly retrieved the extension
ladder from the garage and began to set it up to realign the dish before the game clock
ran out. The edge of the rooftop was located at 20 feet above the ground and she
extended the top of the ladder 3’ above the surface of the rooftop to provide a stable
transition from the ladder to the surface of the roof. As a flat-roofed house with no
eaves, the leading edge of the roof was flush with the side of the house. How far from
the base of the house did Aunt Mavis place the foot of the ladder?
explanation:
Aunt Mavis used the “1 to 4 rule” to determine where to place the foot of the ladder, so
she divided the height of the roof edge by 4 and placed the foot of the ladder 5 feet from
the base of the house.
The correct answer is C.

question:
Monitoring equipment attached to an air compressor that is used to supply a facility’s airline
respirators indicates the concentration of carbon monoxide (CO) in the supply air is 9 ppm.
What is the best course of action by the company?

options.b: Note the level in the maintenance logs
options.c: Monitor the CO levels and begin an investigation on why the levels are at 9 ppm
options.d: Lock-out the compressor to prevent operation until the compressor is serviced

explanation:
Grade D breathing air is used for atmosphere supplying respirators. The ANSI/Compressed
Gas Association Commodity Specification for Air, G-7.1, specifies that Grade D air for supplied
air respirators meet the following limits:
1. Oxygen Content of 19.5-23.5%
2. Hydrocarbon (condensed) content of 5 milligrams per cubic meter of air or less
3. Carbon monoxide (CO) content of 10 ppm or less
4. Carbon dioxide content of 1,000 ppm or less; and
5. Lack of noticeable odor
While 9 ppm of CO is within the standard, it is very close to the limit. It would be imprudent to
ignore the condition.
A reasonable response is to monitor levels to ensure they do not climb above 10 ppm, and
begin an investigation as to what is causing the elevated readings.
The correct answer is C.

The management approach known as “management by objectives” is most frequently
associated with which person?
explanation:
“Management by objectives” is most frequently associated with Peter Drucker, a management
author, in his book The Practice of Management (1954). Management by objectives, or MBO, is

participative development process.

question:

responsibility to ensure that new grinding wheels are properly installed, guarded, and
ready for use when needed. Part of this responsibility involves conducting a “ring test”
on newly received abrasive grinding wheels, immediately prior to their mounting. Which
tool should he use to conduct this test?
explanation:
The “ring test” is explicitly described within OSHA’s Abrasive Wheel Machinery
Standard, 1910.215(d)(1). While the CSP exam is not a regulation-focused test,
occupational safety and health standards are a relatively good source of study material
for common practices and procedures. Many OSHA standards were adopted by
reference or where derived from national consensus standards such as ANSI or NFPA
standards.
The ring test is used to check a new wheel’s structural integrity: an intact wheel will
produce a clear ringing sound when the test is properly conducted.
A good resource for learning more about abrasive wheel machinery is found in Chapter
23 of the National Safety Council’s textbook, Accident Prevention Manual for Business
and Industry (13th Edition), Engineering & Technology.
The correct solution is D.

question:
Joan is a fleet mechanic who is preparing the company service vehicles for what the
weather forecasters have predicted to be a major snowstorm on New Year’s Day. She
is ensuring that the windshield wipers are in good condition and that the windshield
washer fluid reserviors are filled to capacity. She fills the reservoirs with a commercial
washer fluid that is a 50/50 solution of methanol and water with blue dye added as a
colorant. Besides having an odor threshold that is below the more comonly used
occupational exposure limits, methanol exhibits target organ effects of exposure on the:
explanation:
Methanol is toxic to the optic nerve and can cause permanent blindness when ingested
in large quantities. The phrase “blind drunk” has been used to describe the effects of
ingesting adulterated alcoholic beverages. Visual effects from methanol inhalation
exposures are relatively rarely noted in occupational exposure scenarios.
The 8th nerve (the vestibulocochlear nerve) is sometimes referred to as the “auditory
nerve”. Some chemical exposures are associated with ototoxic effects, such as toluene,
an organic solvent.
The stratum corneum is also known as the “horny layer” and comprises the outer
surface of human skin.
The pleura, or “pleural lining” is a two-layered body membrane that lies between the
chest wall and the lungs.
The correct solution is B.

Which material would be most appropriate for use as a shield against beta radiation

question: Which statement best describes the principle of operation employed by a GFCI?

options.a: The GFCI detects minute fluctuations in the conductivity of the neutral wire in an AC circuit, triggering a fast-acting switch that interrupts the supply of electricity.
options.b: The GFCI detects changes in resistance of the supply wire in an AC circuit, triggering a fast-acting switch that interrupts the supply of electricity.
options.c: The GFCI detects line voltage differences between the supply wire and the ground wire in an AC circuit, triggering a fast-acting switch that interrupts the supply of electricity.
options.d: The GFCI detects line amperage differences between the supply wire and the ground wire in an AC circuit, triggering a fast-acting switch that interrupts the supply of electricity.

explanation:
A GFCI, Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter, is sensitive to very small differences in the
amperage (flow of current) on the supply wire of an AC electrical circuit and the
grounded neutral wire, which must be equal in an intact electrical circuit. A difference
between the two wires indicates current leakage, which could represent leakage into a
piece of equipment or into a person. When a difference is sensed by the device, it
triggers a fast-acting switch that interrupts the supply of electricity to the protected
portion of the circuit. The sensitivity of a GFCI is typically around 0.2 mA.
The correct solution is D.

question:
Which type of automatic fire suppression system utilizes sensors within the protected
area in addition to sensors in each sprinkler head to open a valve and fill the distribution
pipe before the sprinkler heads open?
explanation:
A wet-pipe sprinkler system always contains water under pressure.
A dry-pipe sprinkler system is used in locations where freezing can be a problem and so
the system is filled with pressurized gas which, upon opening of a sprinkler head, is
released allowing water to fill the system and be distributed by open sprinkler heads.
A preaction system is a special type of dry-pipe system that utilizes additional sensors
which cause the affected parts of the system to fill with water before the sprinkler heads
open. The advantage of a preaction system over a traditional dry-pipe system is that it
delivers pressurized water to the affected parts of the system more quickly than in a
straight dry-pipe system.
A deluge system has all sprinkler heads open at all times and utilizes sensors within the
protected area to actuate a water valve and deliver water to the open sprinkler heads.
The correct solution is C.

question:

required flow for an emergency eyewash station?

Combination eye/facewash units require a flow of 3.0 gpm (11.4 LPM).
The correct solution is B.

question:
A machine safety improvement project under consideration for financing has anticipated
fixed costs of $17,628 and variable costs of $437.52. The variable costs are incurred
when a protective mechanism engages, forcing a hard-stop to machine operation, which
then requires maintenance services to replace consumable parts and permit resumption
of operations. Over the previous 12 months, the operational fault condition that this
proposed project is expected to resolve has caused 7 serious injuries in 7 separate
instances, incurring average expenses of $1,637.50 per incident. What is the
anticipated payback period for this project? Ignore the time value of money when
answering this question, i.e., assume 0% required return.
explanation:
To solve this no-return pay pack period problem (the required rate of return on this
project is 0%), determine the annual cash flows produced in each 12-month period.
Prevention of losses can be treated as income for purposes of this problem.
Year 1 expense includes the investment expense plus 7 units of variable cost. Year 1
cash generation (income) includes the value of prevention of 7 units of injury (at the
given average expense).
Year 1 = [(-$17,628) + (7 x -$437.52)] + (7 x $1,637.50) = -$9,228.14
Expenses for Year 2 (and for each subsequent year) include the value of 7 units of
variable costs. Year 2 (and after) cash generation (income) includes the value of
prevention of 7 units of injury (at the given average expense).
Year 2 = (7 x -$437.52) + (7 x 1,637.50) = $8,399.86
Payback period is the number of years (not necessarily expressed as an integer) that it
takes to recoup the entire cost of the project, including variable expenses. In this case,
we are ignoring the time-value of money to keep things relatively simple. With the
information we have developed so far, it is easy to estimate the payback period at
something more than 2 and less than 3 years, but to reach the answer we must
determine what fraction of year 3 is needed to achieve payback.
In Year 3 of operation of this project, the project must produce an additional savings of
$828.28 to complete the payback of the project. Divide the amount of additional
required savings by the income generated for the full year to obtain the fractional value
of the year that is needed to arrive at the amount to add to the number of whole years
required (2 years in this case).
n=2 + ($828.28/$8,399.86) = 2.0986 ≈ 2.1 years.
The payback period for this project is 2.1 years.
The correct solution is A.

cash generation (income) includes the value of prevention of 7 units of injury (at the

Year 1 = [(-$17,628) + (7 x -$437.52)] + (7 x $1,637.50) = -$9,228.14
Expenses for Year 2 (and for each subsequent year) include the value of 7 units of
variable costs. Year 2 (and after) cash generation (income) includes the value of
prevention of 7 units of injury (at the given average expense).
Year 2 = (7 x -$437.52) + (7 x 1,637.50) = $8,399.86
Payback period is the number of years (not necessarily expressed as an integer) that it
takes to recoup the entire cost of the project, including variable expenses. In this case,
we are ignoring the time-value of money to keep things relatively simple. With the
information we have developed so far, it is easy to estimate the payback period at
something more than 2 and less than 3 years, but to reach the answer we must
determine what fraction of year 3 is needed to achieve payback.
In Year 3 of operation of this project, the project must produce an additional savings of
$828.28 to complete the payback of the project. Divide the amount of additional
required savings by the income generated for the full year to obtain the fractional value
of the year that is needed to arrive at the amount to add to the number of whole years
required (2 years in this case).
n=2 + ($828.28/$8,399.86) = 2.0986 ≈ 2.1 years.
The payback period for this project is 2.1 years.
The correct solution is A.

CSP Question 6/20/2013 – Machine Guarding
Which type of device controls exposure to amputation hazards by physically limiting the
range of movement of the operators hands or arms?
A. Movable-barrier device
B. Pullback device
C. Restraint device
D. Two-hand control device
Solution:
Restraints may be used on unique and difficult to guard machines. They attach to the
operator’s wrists with wrist-straps and are used to physically limit the movement of the
operator’s hands so as to prevent their entry into the point of operation at any time.

CSP Question 6/27/2013 – Fire Safety
What is the key difference between a detonation and a deflagration?
A. Speed of the resultant concussive wave-front
B. Rate of reaction within the subject material
C. Amount of pressure generated within the surrounding environment
D. Degree of confinement or enclosure around the subject material
Solution:
Deflagrations and detonations are general classifiations of types of combustion
explosions produced by some exothermic chemical reactions. A chemical reaction that
results in a deflagration has a rate of reaction that is slower than that of one that
produces a detonation. A deflagration will not always produce sufficiently rapid
increases of pressure to produce what would be recognized as an “explosion”, but a
detonation typically does produce an explosion. The primary difference between a
deflagration and a detonation is the rate of reaction within the subject material.
For more on explosions and their hazards, refer to Chapter 17 of Safety and Health for
Engineers (2nd edition), by Roger L. Brauer.
The correct solution is B.
CSP Question 7/4/2013 – Material Handling
As the angle formed by the legs of a sling increases, what happens to the tension on
each leg of the sling?
A. Increases
B. Decreases
C. Stays the same
D. Becomes equal with the other leg
Solution:
As the angle of the legs of a sling increases (becomes wider), the tension on the legs of
the sling increases, resulting in a decreased carrying capacity of the sling. Stated
differently, as the angle between the legs increases, the carrying capacity of the sling is
reduced. A sling where both legs are vertical is strongest; a sling where the legs form a
60 degree angle has a 50% lower carrying capacity.
Reference: NSC Accident Prevention Manual for Business and Industry: Engineering
and Technology (11th Edition), CH 16, Figure 16-12, p493-494.
The correct solution is A.

carcinogen.

http://www.osha.gov/Publications/3371combustible-dust.pdf , and
http://www.cdc.gov/niosh/npg/npgd0552.html

CSP Question 7/18/2013 – Basic Science
The drybulb temperature is 87ºF and the wet bulb temperature is 65ºF. What is the
approximate relative humidity under these conditions?
A. 30%
B. 40%
C. 50%
D. 60%
Solution:
To determine the relative humidity given the drybulb and wetbulb temperatures, find the
intersection of the vertical line extending from the drybulb temperature reading to the
diagonal wet bulb reading line. The RH contours form arcs across the graph.
The following excerpt is from OSHA heat stress guidance at:
http://www.osha.gov/SLTC/heatillness/heat_index/about.html
“Relative humidity is a measure of the amount of moisture in the air. Sweat does not
evaporate as quickly when the air is moist as it does in a dry climate. Since evaporation
of sweat from the skin is one of the ways the human body cools itself on a hot day, high
humidity reduces our natural cooling potential and we feel hotter. Low humidity can also
be a problem for outdoor workers in hot, desert-like climates. Sweat evaporates very
rapidly in low humidity, which can lead to severe dehydration if a person does not drink
enough water throughout the day.”
Image Source: http://www.bcsp.org/pdf/ASPCSP/CP_ExamRef.pdf , page 5
The correct solution is A.

CSP Question 8/15/2013 – Ergonomics
Finklestein's test is used to diagnose:
A. Blood lead concentrations
B. Epicondylitis

Solution:
Finklestein’s test is one approach used by a physician to diagnose DeQuervain’s
tenosynovitis, a musculoskeltal disorder of the wrist. It is performed by the physician

Work related risk factors for the occurrence of DeQuervain’s include combined forceful
gripping and twisting motions.

CSP Question 8/29/2013 – Radiation
Which type of radioactive source poses the greatest exposure hazard?
A. Powdered alpha source
B. Solid beta source
C. Liquid beta source
D. Solid gamma source
Solution:
Generally a solid source poses less of an exposure hazard than is a liquid or a
powdered/particulate source material. A solid can be relatively easily contained,
shielded, and protected, whereas a liquid source can splash, spread, absorb and/or be
ingested. A powdered source has the added potential to be readily inhaled if disturbed.
A gaseous source (such as naturally occurring radon gas) can also be readily inhaled,
but can also be rapidly evacuated from a contaminated area.
Each of the sources pose exposure hazards which can be influenced by a number of
different factors, including their radioactive “activity level”. However, given the answer
choices, the best answer is Choice A, a powdered alpha source.
Alpha particles are the largest and heaviest form of ionizing radiation, but they do not
travel very far in air. They are effectively stopped by the outer layer of the skin or a
sheet of paper. Their primary hazard is as an internal hazard, where close contact with
sensitive body tissues may result in adverse health effects.
Beta particles are essentially free electrons that can be effectively shielded with use of
low-density materials such as aluminum foil or acrylic “glass” (Lexan and Plexiglass are
specific example brand names of acrylic material). If energetic Beta particles interact
with high-density shielding materials, such as lead or steel, secondary radiation that is
similar to X-ray radiation can be produced. This secondary radiation is known as
Bremmstrahlung.
Gamma sources produce electromagnetic (vs. energetic particle) emissions. Shielding
for gamma sources typically utilizes a high-density material, such as lead.
The correct solution is A.
CSP Question 9/5/2013 – Management
When establishing performance goals with direct-reporting staff members, which factor
is most important?
A. Creating a mutually agreed upon description of acceptable performance
B. Creating a mutually agreed upon completion date
C. Creating a mutually agreed upon budget for use while pursuing the goal
D. Creating a mutually agreed upon tactical plan to achieve the goal
Solution:
Goals, when properly constructed, can be tremendously motivating and helpful for
employees and their organizations.
The most essential element of the process of establishing performance goals is for the
manager and subbordinate to arrive at an agreement as to what constitutes “acceptable
performance” each goal statement. To avoid ambiguity, assumptions, and
misinterpretations, it is generally best for the employee and the organization if the
agreed-upon description of acceptable performance for each goal is reduced to writing.
Most general management textbooks devote at least a few pages to discussion of goal-
setting. One timeless and particularly good reference on goal-setting is Goal Setting, A
Motivational Technique That Works, by Edwin A. Locke and Gary P. Latham (1984),
Prentice-Hall, Inc.
The correct solution is A.

question:
A computer controlling a critical process system must have continuous power. The
main power source is supplied from the local utility via overhead powerlines. The plant
has a backup diesel generator to supply power when the local utility has an outage.
The computer has a backup battery to supply power if both the utility and diesel
generator go down.
The plant has a 0.005 probability of suffering a local power outage on any given day.
The diesel generator has a 0.0001 probability of failing on any given day. The battery
backup has a 0.00001 probability of failing on any given day.
What is the probability the computer will lose power on any given day in one year?
explanation:
The total probability of 3 independent events happening is the product of each event.
Thus the probability of total failure today is given by
P(failure today) = (0.005) x (0.0001) x (0.00001) = 0.000000000005 = 5 x 10-12
The probability of no failure today is given by
P(no failure today) =1 – P(failure today) = 1 – (5 x 10-12) = 0.999999999995
The question asks for the probability of no failure for 365 successive days. There are
365 independent events multiplied together. Probability of no failure for 365 days is
given by
P(no failure for 1 year) = [1-(5 x 10-12)]365 = 0.999999998175
The probability of at least one failure is given by
P(at least one failure in 1 year) = 1 – P(no failure for 1 year)
= 1 - [1-(5 x 10-12)]365 = 0.000000001825
The correct solution is B.
Page 2 of 2

question:

(explosion) and working backwards in the process to determine all the possible
scenarios that could lead to the explosion.

process and uses management processes to minimize risk.

happening simultaneously.

components fail in the process. It starts with a failure and moves forward in time to the
consequence.

process to look at all event sequences that may lead to the catastrophic events. A fault
tree is created with the roots of the tree leading to the catastrophic event at the top.

question:
A worker is using a full-body harness while working at an elevation of 200 ft above
grade. The worker slips and falls, but his lanyard and harness stop him after falling
about 6 feet. Unfortunately, the worker is unconscious. How long can the worker safely
hang in the harness without becoming a fatality?
explanation:
A worker hanging from a harness, (especially one that is unconscious), is at great risk of
suffering from orthostatic intolerance. This is a condition caused by poor circulation of
the blood. A very brief explanation of what happens is that the blood that has not
circulated has very low oxygen levels. When the person is moved, and the blood starts
to circulate again, the blood with low oxygen levels can cause major problems (even
death).
A better explanation is found on the OSHA website
http://www.osha.gov/dts/shib/shib032404.pdf.
Companies using a harness as fall protection need to have a plan to rescue workers
quickly if they’ve fallen.
The correct solution is B.

question:
An industrial process is composed of unit A, unit B, unit C, and unit D. The process
needs either a functioning unit A or a functioning unit B to operate. Unit C and unit D
must also be functioning for the process to operate. The probability that unit A will fail
during a ten-year period is 0.01. The probability that unit B will fail during a one-year
period is 0.001. The probability that unit C will fail in a five-year period is 0.00001. The
probability of unit D failing during a ten-year period is 10-7.
What is the probability the industrial process will fail during a ten-year period?
explanation:
The probability of A failing during 10 years is 0.01.
The probability of B failing during 10 years is 1-0.99910 = 9.96 x 10-3 ≅ 0.01
The probability of both A and B failing during 10 years is 0.01 x 0.01 = 10-4.
The probability of C failing during 10 years is 1 – 0.999992 ≅ 2 x 10-5.
The probability of D failing during 10 years is 10-7.
The probability of the process failing during 10 years
is 10-4 + 2 x 10 -5 + 10-7 ≅ 10-4.
The correct solution is D.

question:
A woman was severely injured (3rd degree burns) several years ago when she spilled
coffee on her lap she had just purchased from a restaurant. She sued the restaurant to
recover the costs of her medical bills. The company was held liable for the woman’s
damages by the court.
What theory of liability did the company violate?

options.d: None of the above is correct. The company was not actually liable

explanation:
Plaintiffs in a product liability lawsuit must show that the product was defective, the
defect existed when it left the defendant’s hands, and the defect caused the injury or
harm.
Warranty liability includes merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. Implied
warranty is a branch of contract law. Merchantability applies to companies that normally
offer a product. There is an implied warranty that the product meets some level of
quality and is safe to use.
Negligence lawsuits must show the defendant had a duty to provide a product free of
the claimed defect and was negligent in performing that duty. Negligence is a behavior
and can be difficult to prove.
A manufacturer is strictly liable in tort when the company sold a product with a defect
and the defect caused an injury. It does not deal with the behavior of the company.
The best solution is C.
B is also a possible solution, but we would need to know more information before
determining negligence.

Solution:

question: What is the major injury from electrical arc flashes?
explanation:
A tremendous amount of energy is released during an arc flash. Employees exposed to
arc flashes frequently receive very severe burns.
The correct solution is B.

question:
Wire rope is used in many applications. A common wire rope fitting is to use U-bolts to
attach the dead end of the rope to the load-bearing section of the rope. What is the
proper way to attach the U-bolts to the wire rope?

options.a: The U section of each clip is on the live (long end) of the rope.
options.b: The U section of each clip is on the dead (short end) of the rope.
options.c: The U sections should alternate on the rope (live-dead-live).
options.d: The U sections should alternate on the rope (dead-live-live).

explanation:
The U section of each clip should be on the dead (short end) of the rope. Remember
the saying “never saddle a dead horse.”
The correct solution is B.

NRR that will provide adequate protection in compliance with the OSHA PEL?
explanation:

104 – 90 = 14
The correct solution is A.

question: Select the true statement relating to behavior-based safety processes.

options.a: Behavior-based safety is based on Maslow’s hierarchy of needs.
options.b: Behavior-based safety is a management driven process.
options.c: Behavior-based safety is focused on the correct discipline of employees violating safety procedures.
options.d: None of the above statements is true.

explanation:
Behavior-based safety is based on the measurement of safe behaviors in the
workplace. It is an employee-driven process that will only succeed with the active
participation of employees.
The correct solution is D.

question:
Which type of machine guarding technique requires the least amount of participation
from employees?
explanation:
Pullout devices and physical restraints require employees to fit themselves to the
devices and wear them.
Devices requiring two hand controls for operation may be defeated by employees by
forcing one control to be continuously turned on.
The correct solution is D.

question: Which type of shielding material is appropriate for beta radiation?
explanation:
Bremsstrahlung radiation results when beta particles interact with materials of high
atomic numbers.
The correct solution is A.

question: Which waste stream is okay to dispose with incineration?
explanation:
Cadmium, lead and radioactive waste are essentially unchanged with incineration.
Incineration of these materials is likely to spread the contaminants over a wide area.
Benzene is a volatile organic compound, and it is very easy to burn.
The correct solution is B.

question:
A well maintained fire suppression system uses wet-pipe sprinklers to control fires in an
office building. The sprinklers are designed to allow water flow when the temperature
of the sprinkler head reaches 100 F. There is a drop-down ceiling in the office building,
and many of the panels in the ceiling have been removed. How is the removal of the
ceiling panels likely to affect the sprinkler head operation?

options.a: The sprinklers are likely to respond more quickly to a fire.
options.b: The sprinklers are likely to respond more slowly to a fire.
options.c: The sprinklers are unaffected by the removal of ceiling panels.
options.d: There is not enough information to correctly answer this question.

explanation:
The hot gases and smoke from a fire will rise past the sprinkler head and collect above
the ceiling panels. It will take longer for the sprinkler heard to reach 100 F.
The correct solution is B.

What is an appropriate bench height for work that predominantly involves the use of
upper body strength from a standing position?
explanation:
Delicate work with the hands at a standing workstation should have the bench set 2 to 4
inches above elbow height.
Manual work using tools at a standing workstation should have the bench set 4 to 6
inches below elbow height.
Work that requires the use of upper body strength at a standing workstation should
have the bench set 6 to 16 inches below elbow height.
The correct solution is D.

crane. The worker is using a 20 ft sling to attach the equipment to the crane’s hook.

using the sling?

options.a: Single leg with sling hanging straight down.

explanation:
The vertical basket hitch almost doubles the lifting capacity of the sling. Each leg of the
sling is able to carry the weight of a single leg.
The correct solution is D.

question:
An envelope containing a white powder is opened in an office. The white powder may
be anthrax spores. Which response is most likely to minimize risks?

options.a: Set the HVAC on maximum airflow to bring in fresh air.
options.b: Shut down the airflow through the HVAC system.
options.c: Set the HVAC on the maximum temperature setting.
options.d: Set the HVAC on the minimum temperature setting.

explanation:
Risk will be minimized by keeping the powder as localized as possible. Shutting down
the HVAC system will keep spores from being spread throughout the workplace.
The correct solution is B.

question:
An office worker uses two power strips daisy chained in series to power a printer, a
computer, and a computer monitor. The power strips are protected by fuses. Why is this
considered an unsafe practice?

options.a: Too much current is being drawn through the power strips.
options.b: Too much voltage is being drawn through the power strips.
options.c: The power strips are not grounded properly.
options.d: This practice violates the UL listing of the power strips.

explanation:
Power strips are designed to be plugged directly into a wall receptacle. The practice
violates the usage of the UL approval.
The correct solution is D.

question:
Airborne silica particles are hazardous to human health. Which particulate size is most
hazardous to health?
explanation:
Smaller particles will penetrate deeper into the lungs. Respirable particles are those
that are deposited in the alveoli. About 50% of 4 micron particles are respirable.
Particles deposited into the alveoli cause the greatest damage to human health.
The correct solution is A.

Natural fiber materials are preferred personal protective equipment for persons

question: Which of the following is a bacterial biohazard?
explanation:
Ebola is a virus.
Histoplasmosis is caused by a fungus.
Legionella is a bacteria.
Hookworm is a parasite.

deviation of the test scores is 24. Assume the test scores are normally distributed, and
estimate the test score of the 5th percentile.
explanation:
Use the z-table to determine the number of standard deviations below the mean that
provides the 5th percentile.

question: Select the correct statement.

options.a: Safety management is primarily an educational problem.
options.b: Safety management is primarily an enforcement problem.
options.c: Safety management is primarily an engineering problem.
options.d: Safety management is primarily a motivational problem.

explanation:
Dan Petersen discusses the current research and the history of safety management in
his book Safety Management: A Human Approach published by the American Society of
Safety Engineers.
Dr. Petersen explains that traditional safety management was focused on the three E’s
(engineering, enforcement, and education). He clearly states that safety is a people
problem, and all safety depends on motivation.
The correct solution is D.

question: What type of fire extinguisher rating is appropriate for a restaurant kitchen?
explanation:
Class A fires are fueled by ordinary combustibles such as paper, wood, and cloth.
Class B fires are fueled by liquids such as paint and oil.
Class C fires involved electrified equipment such as electric motors.
Class D fires are fueled by solid metals such as potassium and sodium.
Class K fires are fueled by cooking oils and greases.
The correct solution is A.

question:
Ethylene oxide has a short term exposure limit of 5 ppm. The PEL is 1 ppm, and the
action limit is 0.5 ppm. What type of sampling is appropriate to ensure employees are
not exceeding the short term exposure limit?

options.a: Use a passive dosimeter for a full shift on the employee that is expected to have the highest exposure.
options.b: Use a passive dosimeter on the employee that is expected to have the highest exposure for 15 minutes during the activity that is most likely to have the highest exposure.
options.c: Use a personal sampling pump for a full shift on the employee that is expected to have the highest exposure.
options.d: Use a personal sampling pump on the employee that is expected to have the highest exposure for 15 minutes during the activity that is most likely to have the highest exposure.

explanation:
Passive dosimeters may be used for full shift samples, but they do not work quickly
enough to determine short term exposures.
The correct solution is D.

question:
The circuit breakers in an electrical panel will trip when the amperage through the circuit
exceeds the rating of the breaker. This feature protects from which hazard?

options.c: Damage to the electrical distribution system

explanation:
Circuit breakers protect circuits from high current. High current can cause the wires to
overheat. Circuit breakers protect from fire.
The correct solution is D.

question:
A process uses a resin with a very low vapor pressure at room temperatures. The resin
has a relatively high exposure limit. The work is performed at 2 stations along a wall of
the process room. The mixing factor in the room is 12. Which engineering control is
most appropriate?
explanation:
The canopy hood is appropriate for processes that have momentum carrying the
contaminant vertically to the hood.
The downdraft table pulls air directly from the process into the table.
Dilution ventilation is useful for contaminants with low toxicity (i.e. high exposure limits)
and when the costs of make-up air are not excessive. It is typically used for multiple
sources or sources that are mobile and where there is good mixing. A mixing factor of
12 indicates very poor mixing in the room.
Glove boxes are used for highly hazardous substances.
The correct solution is B.

question: What is the purpose of a histogram?

options.a: A histogram is used to set the 95% confidence interval for the mean.
options.b: A histogram is used to diagram the data distribution.
options.c: A histogram is used to evaluate the history of repeated measures.
options.d: A histogram is used to determine the critical value of a t-test.

explanation:
A histogram is a graphical representation of the data distribution.
The correct solution is B.

Hazard and Operability (HAZOP) Studies
Background.
A HAZOP study identifies hazards and operability problems. The concept involves investigating how the plant might
deviate from the design intent. If, in the process of identifying problems during a HAZOP study, a solution becomes
apparent, it is recorded as part of the HAZOP result; however, care must be taken to avoid trying to find solutions which
are not so apparent, because the prime objective for the HAZOP is problem identification. Although the HAZOP study
was developed to supplement experience based practices when a new design or technology is involved, its use has
expanded to almost all phases of a plant's life. HAZOP is based on the principle that several experts with different
backgrounds can interact and identify more problems when working together than when working separately and
combining their results. The "Guide-Word" HAZOP is the most well known of the HAZOPs; however, several
specialisations of this basic method have been developed.
Concept.
The HAZOP concept is to review the plant in a series of meetings, during which a multidisciplinary team methodically
"brainstorms" the plant design, following the structure provided by the guide words and the team leader's experience.
The primary advantage of this brainstorming is that it stimulates creativity and generates ideas. This creativity results
from the interaction of the team and their diverse backgrounds. Consequently the process requires that all team
members participate (quantity breeds quality in this case), and team members must refrain from criticizing each other to
the point that members hesitate to suggest ideas. The team focuses on specific points of the design (called "study
nodes"), one at a time. At each of these study nodes, deviations in the process parameters are examined using the
guide words. The guide words are used to ensure that the design is explored in every conceivable way. Thus the team
must identify a fairly large number of deviations, each of which must then be considered so that their potential causes
and consequences can be identified. The best time to conduct a HAZOP is when the design is fairly firm. At this point,
the design is well enough defined to allow meaningful answers to the questions raised in the HAZOP process. Also, at
this point it is still possible to change the design without a major cost. However, HAZOPs can be done at any stage
after the design is nearly firm. For example, many older plants are upgrading their control and instrumentation systems.
The success or failure of the HAZOP depends on several factors:
• The completeness and accuracy of drawings and other data used as a basis for the study
• The technical skills and insights of the team
• The ability of the team to use the approach as an aid to their imagination in visualizing deviations, causes, and
consequences
• The ability of the team to concentrate on the more serious hazards which are identified.
The process is systematic and it is helpful to define the terms that are used:
a. STUDY NODES - The locations (on piping and instrumentation drawings and procedures) at which the process
parameters are investigated for deviations.
b. INTENTION - The intention defines how the plant is expected to operate in the absence of deviations at the study
nodes. This can take a number of forms and can either be descriptive or diagrammatic; e.g., flowsheets, line diagrams,
P&IDS.
c. DEVIATIONS - These are departures from the intention which are discovered by systematically applying the guide
words (e.g., "more pressure").
d. CAUSES - These are the reasons why deviations might occur. Once a deviation has been shown to have a credible
cause, it can be treated as a meaningful deviation. These causes can be hardware failures, human errors, an
unanticipated process state (e.g., change of composition), external disruptions (e.g., loss of power), etc.
e. CONSEQUENCES - These are the results of the deviations should they occur (e.g., release of toxic materials).
Trivial consequences, relative to the study objective, are dropped.
f. GUIDE WORDS - These are simple words which are used to qualify or quantify the intention in order to guide and
stimulate the brainstorming process and so discover deviations. The guide words shown in the following table are the
ones most often used in a HAZOP; some organisations have made this list specific to their operations, to guide the team
more quickly to the areas where they have previously found problems. Each guide word is applied to the process
variables at the point in the plant (study node) which is being examined.
HAZOP GUIDE WORDS AND MEANINGS
Guide Word Meaning
No Negation of the Design Intent
Less Quantitative Decrease
More Quantitative Increase
Part Of Qualitative Decrease
As Well As Qualitative Increase
Reverse Logical Opposite of the Intent
Other Than Complete Substitution
These guide words are applicable to both the more general parameters (e.g. react, transfer) and to the more specific
parameters (e.g. pressure, temperature, flow). With the general parameters, meaningful deviations are usually
generated for each guide word. Moreover, it is not unusual to have more than one deviation from the application of one
guide word. For example, "more reaction" could mean either that a reaction takes place at a faster rate, or that a
greater quantity of product results.
With the specific parameters, some modification of the guide words may be necessary. In addition, it is not unusual to
find that some potential deviations are eliminated by physical limitation. For example, if the design intention of a
pressure or temperature is being considered, the guide words “more” or "less" may be the only possibilities.
Finally, when dealing with a design intention involving a complex set of interrelated plant parameters (e.g.,
temperatures, reaction rates, composition, or pressure), it may be better to apply the whole sequence of guide words to
each parameter individually than to apply each guide word across all of the parameters as a group. Also, when applying
the guide words to a sentence it may be more useful to apply the sequence of guide words to each word or phrase
separately, starting with the key part which describes the activity (usually the verbs or adverbs). These parts of the
sentence usually are related to some impact on the process parameters.
Guidelines for Using Procedure
The concepts presented above are put into practice in the following steps:
1. Define the purpose, objectives, and scope of the study
2. Select the team
3.- Prepare for the study
4. Carry out the team review
5. Record the results.
6. Follow up to ensure results are implemented.
It is important to recognize that some of these steps can take place at the same time. For example, the team reviews
the design, records the findings, and follows up on the findings continuously.
(Refer also to the diagrammatic representation of the HAZOP procedure attached).

The HAZOP Report
Aims
The report should provide sufficient information on each element so that, either read alone or together
with available and clearly cross referenced documents, an assessment can be made of the adequacy of
the HAZOP study carried out.
Title Page
The study title should be displayed both on the cover and on a separate title sheet. The title should
clearly and unambiguously identify the facility covered by the Study. The title page should also show the
type of operation, whether it is a proposed operation or an existing facility and its location.
The title sheet should specify on whose authority the report was prepared and the date it was authorised.
The name/s/ of the chairperson and organisation she or he represents should be stated.
Table of Contents
A table of contents should be included at the beginning of the report. It should include a list of figures,
tables and appendices.
Glossary and Abbreviations
A glossary of any special terms or titles and a list of abbreviations should be included to ensure that the
report can be readily and clearly understood.
Summary of Main Findings and Recommendations
This Summary should briefly outline the nature of the proposal or existing facility and the scope of the
report. A list of the main conclusions and recommendations arising from the HAZOP should be
presented. An indicative implementation timetable is also useful.
Scope of Report
This section should give a brief description of the aims and purpose of the study and the reason for its
preparation. For example, is the study being prepared to satisfy conditions of development consent or at
the company's initiative as part of safety upgrading? Is it for an entirely new development or for the
modification of, or extension to, an existing development? Reference should be made to any other
relevant safety related studies completed or under preparation.
Description of the Facility
This section should give an overview of the site, plant and materials used/stored. Where this information
is already available through an EIS, hazard analysis or other document, clear cross reference to these
documents or inclusion in the form of appendices would suffice.
The description should include: a) Site locational sketch with identification of adjacent/surrounding land
uses. b) A schematic diagram of the plant under study along with a brief description of each process
step involved. The location and nature of raw materials and product storage should also be shown as
well as loading/unloading facilities. The plant does not have to be described in detail, though some
process conditions such as pressure in pressurised vessels may be necessary to gain an understanding
of the plant. c) Clearly identified P&IDs with plant and line numbers as used in the HAZOP.
Instrumentation and equipment symbols should be explained. Alternatives used (photographs, plans,
etc.) should also carry appropriate identification. Where a large number of P&IDs are involved in the
study, only those relevant to the recommendations need be appended to the report.
HAZOP Team Members
This section should list the HAZOP participants, together with their affiliations and positions. Their
responsibility, qualifications, and relevant experience should also be given. The chairperson and the
secretary of the group should also each be identified. The dates of the meetings and their duration
should be provided. Where some members were not present at all meetings, the extent of their
participation should be indicated. Special visitors and occasional members should be listed in a manner
similar to the continuing members, with the reasons for their attendance detailed. For example,
specialist instrumentation engineer/consultants may be required to overcome specific design problems.
HAZOP Methodology
The general approach used should be briefly outlined. Any changes to the accepted standard
methodology used for a HAZOP should be detailed and explained.
Guide Words
The guide words used to identify possible deviations in this HAZOP should be listed. An explanation of
any specialised words used for the facility should also be given.
Plant Overview
This section should outline what general conditions and situations likely to result in a potentially
hazardous outcome were considered in the HAZOP (following line by line analysis) for the overall P&ID
or section including overview issues, such as:
• first start-up procedures
• emergency shutdown procedures
• alarms and instrumentation trip testing
• pre-commissioning operator training
• plant protection systems
• failure of services
• breakdowns
• effluent (gas, liquid, solid/
• noise.
Any issues raised and considered necessary for review outside the HAZOP should be detailed.
A set of overview guide words is included in Appendix 1.
Analysis of Main Findings
An indication of the criteria used to determine whether or not action was chosen to be taken regarding
the outcome of a deviation is required.
The results of the HAZOP, giving deviations, consequences and actions required, should be provided.
Those events on which the decision of no action was made should also be listed, along with the events
for which consequence or risk analysis was considered necessary. The decisions made after such
further analyses should also be given. Any alternative actions generated and considered should be
detailed.
Actions Arising from the HAZOP
This section should highlight those actions which are potentially hazardous to plant personnel, the public
or the environment or have the potential to jeopardise the operability of the plant. Also included should
be a clear statement of commitment to modify the design or operational procedures in accordance with
the identified required actions and a timetable for implementation. Justification as to why no action was
chosen for any actions identified should also be made. The current status of the recommended actions
at the time of the report should also be given together with the names/designations of persons
responsible for their implementation.
